extra.message: SSRF via webhook delivery bypassing safe-URL check through HTTP redirect — Server-side request forgery allowing an attacker (an ops_admin registering a malicious/compromised webhook URL, or a webhook host that later starts redirecting) to reach internal-only services and cloud metadata endpoints from the backend, potentially exfiltrating instance credentials or hitting internal admin APIs [verified: Same root cause: the resolved-safe check at enqueue_event's _is_safe_url call is not enforced on redirect targets used by urlopen at line 84, allowing an ops_admin-registered webhook to SSRF via redirect.]

SSRF via webhook test endpoint bypassing safe-URL check through HTTP redirect — Same as above: internal network / metadata service access triggered on-demand via the Test button in the webhooks admin UI [verified: test_webhook has the identical pattern — _is_safe_url(hook.url) checked once, then urlopen at line 127 follows redirects unchecked, reachable via the admin Test-webhook action.]

Hardcoded default secret_key fallback — If deployed without overriding SECRET_KEY, any HMAC/signature or cryptographic use of this value becomes forgeable by anyone who knows the public default. [verified: secret_key has a hardcoded, publicly-known default at config.py:9 with no runtime check forcing an override, so any deployment forgetting to set SECRET_KEY has forgeable session/HMAC signatures.]

Session cookie not Secure by default — Session token can be intercepted via network MITM or HTTP downgrade, leading to session hijacking and account takeover of any role including ops_admin. [verified: cookie_secure defaults to False at config.py:13 and flows to secure=settings.cookie_secure in auth.py, so unless operators override the env var the session cookie ships without Secure, enabling MITM interception.]
